test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 18 Sept 2022 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: If two parallel lines are intersected by a transversal, then which of the options below is not necessarily correct?

options.text: A pair of interior angles on the same side of the transversal have the same measure.
A pair of corresponding angles have the same measure.
A pair of alternate interior angles have the same measure.
A pair of vertically opposite angles have the same measure.

solution:
**Given:**

Let AB and CD be parallel lines.

PQ is a transverse line that intersects parallel lines.

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d52466df1a39d389d02f57c0bea92ddbc060611643ccbde44c59681716b4ecbb.png] **

**Concept and Solution:**

 
• **Corresponding angles:** Corresponding angles are **the angles that are formed in matching corners or corresponding corners with the transversal when two parallel lines are intersected by any other line**

 
 
• **​angle4=angle8\ angle3=angle7\ angle1=angle5\ angle2=angle6**
 
 
 
• **Alternate interior angles: **Alternate interior angles are the **angles formed when a transversal intersects two coplanar lines**. They lie on the inner side of the parallel lines but on the opposite sides of the transversal. The transversal crosses through the two lines which are Coplanar at separate points.
 
 
• ​angle4=angle6\ angle3=angle5
 
 
 
• **Vertically opposite angles: **A pair of vertically opposite angles are always equal.
 
 
• angle6=angle8\ angle5=angle7\ angle1=angle3\ angle2=angle4
 
 
 
• **Sum of alternate interior angles of the same side: **Sum of alternate interior angles of the same side is 180°.
 
 
• angle5+angle4=180⁰\\angle6+angle3=180⁰
 
 

Option 1 does not match these definitions.

Hence, 'A pair of interior angles on the same side of the transversal have the same measure' is not necessarily correct.

1f
